_comment: Single source of truth for all configurable parameters in spec.md. Roles read this; nothing re-derives these values independently. See harness spec.md Generation Rules for this requirement.

cities._note: spec #2 -- city names unique per game, duplicates reassigned to a geographically close alternative (never silently allowed to collide), players may still pick freely. The data and the resolution procedure live in content/gazetteer.json; these are the knobs that procedure reads.

content._note: spec #13, #33 -- seeded game content lives in content/ and is extended by players during play, not re-derived per role. newspaper_file holds The Daily Manifest's own copy: mastheads, department frames, the wire styles, image palettes and the tone register. It is content for the same reason the phrasing ladder is -- the wordings are writing decisions, and the renderer is their implementation.

rounds._note: one round timer for the whole game; every round advances import-open, export-close, and winner-resolution in lockstep (spec #9-#12)

imports._note: spec #13, #13a, #14, #22 -- same category may go to different cities but not to the same city twice, by default. reuse_same_need_within_game governs the individual need rather than its category: with 48 seeds and at most 20 needs in a maximum game, replaying the exact same brief verbatim is never necessary, so it is off.
imports._choice_note: spec #13 (user decision, 2026-08-31): the importing mayor chooses their city's next import, so nothing here selects one. suggestions_offered_to_importer is the size of the slate of eligible seeds put in front of them -- 'a small set', large enough to be a choice and small enough to read in a message; the slate spreads across categories before it doubles up, and a mayor may also name an eligible seed that is not on it. choice_offered_rounds_ahead is how many rounds before their turn the check-in asks for the order, and it is 1 because spec #13 says to ask 'on the city's actual import turn, not prematurely'. A round's needs open before its check-ins do, so the check-in that belongs to a city's import turn is the last one before it -- one round ahead, and no more. At 1, a mayor in a three-city game is asked every three rounds, which is the cadence spec #13 names; at 2 they were asked twice per rotation, two rounds early, planning a turn that had not come round. 0 asks only once the queue is already holding the turn open, which costs a round of the game per turn and is why it is not the default. Whatever the value, an order due in the same check-in as a pick and an eligible export is deferred rather than allowed to displace the export (spec #11a); see engine/game.py's DEFERRABLE_GAME_ACTIONS. unchosen_turn_grace_rounds is how many rounds the queue holds an unfiled turn open before passing over it -- the round opens no need at all while it waits, because opening one nobody ordered is the thing spec #13 exists to stop, and a turn that is never filed is lost with no other penalty (spec #16's reading of a no-show, applied to the import side). There is deliberately no knob for 'accept freeform requests' or 'let the engine pick': spec #13 requires the first and forbids the second, and config.json holds the parameters of the rules, not switches for them.

exports._note: spec #15. importer_may_export_to_own_need is not settled by the spec either way; false is the sane default because a mayor exporting to their own import need would be judging their own entry, which blind voting (spec #18) cannot survive. Exposed rather than hardcoded so a facilitator can decide otherwise.

economy._note: spec #20-#22 -- exposure policy is intentionally config-driven so it can be iterated on; non-winning submission origin must never be exposed regardless of this config (spec #21, not overridable, and deliberately absent from this file: engine/economy.py holds it as a constant and tests/test_economy.py fails if a knob for it ever appears here). profit_roll is parsed as NdS rather than assumed to be two six-sided dice. even_split_mode decides what spec #19's 'split evenly' means when the roll does not divide cleanly: 'exact_fraction' (each city gets total/n exactly, the parts sum to the whole) or 'floor_discard_remainder' (integer-only ledgers, remainder unawarded). Every value in this block is validated when a game is constructed, not at the first roll, so a typo here refuses to start a game rather than crashing it three rounds in.

facilitator_questions._max_per_player_note: How many of a mayor's two check-in slots may be a question. Spec #23 allows at most one, so the engine accepts 1 (ask) or 0 (suppress questions for a mayor while leaving the round's question asked of others) and refuses anything higher rather than silently capping it.
facilitator_questions._note: spec #23-#25; scope is configurable for a future domain-specific harness run (e.g. 'coding_preferences'). ask_every_n_rounds is spec #23's 'not every round necessarily needs a question' -- 1 asks every round, 2 every other round, and `enabled: false` never. One question per round is asked of every mayor who checks in, because aggregate phrasing ('the world', 'some countries') is only meaningful when everyone was asked the same thing.

prose._note: renderer names a writer registered in newspaper/prose.py. 'deterministic_template' assembles each edition from content/newspaper.json's frames and the round's actual facts: no network, no provider, reproducible from the game seed, and every sentence a checkable function of game state -- which is what lets tests assert that an aggregate claim is true of its distribution (spec #25) rather than merely well-phrased. A future model-backed writer registers alongside it under its own id and is selected here; the interface it must satisfy is `write(edition_context) -> departments`. max_declined_exports_printed caps how many non-winning exports an Arrivals column reprints; their origin city is never printed at any setting (spec #21) and an export whose own text names a city is withheld instead of reprinted.

image._note: spec #29 and the user decision of 2026-08-24: a fun, colorful raster image is preferred, and a deterministic, game-state-informed SVG is an explicitly permitted fallback when no raster provider is available. modality_preference is that policy, in order. raster_providers names adapters registered in newspaper/imagery.py; it is empty because this deployment has no image-generation provider, so every edition falls back to svg_procedural and says so in its own image.provenance. Naming a provider that is not registered is a config error rather than a silent fallback -- a facilitator who wires up a provider should hear about a typo, not quietly get SVGs.

output._note: Where a rendered edition lands on disk, as files to read in the repository. Serving the same editions at the paper's unguessable, noindex URL with the archive browsable (spec #26, #27) is the separate `hosting` block below; it renders the edition payloads to HTML itself rather than reading these files, so neither output is downstream of the other.

newspaper._note: spec #26-#30; player_identity_style may later support more anonymity per decisions Q26. The four tone flags are load-bearing, not decorative: `funny` false drops the editorial asides and leaves the paper reporting facts, `colorful` false switches the edition image to the monochrome palette, `allow_pointed_humor` false filters out every frame content marks `pointed`, and `disallow_snide_or_mean` runs content/newspaper.json's forbidden register over the finished prose and refuses to publish an edition that trips it.
newspaper._tone_scope_note: spec #30b. forbidden_register_scope says whose prose that register grades, and `newspaper_voice` is the only value this paper implements: the desk is answerable for its own copy, while a passage a mayor typed -- a free-form export (spec #15), an answer to a mayoral question -- is printed exactly as typed, marked as that mayor's words by content/newspaper.json's player_voice lines, and subtracted from the scan (newspaper/voice.py). The key is stated here rather than assumed in code because scope is a policy, and refused rather than defaulted if it says anything else, because the alternative -- grading players by the desk's register -- means an adjective in one mayor's offer stops the whole table's round.

facilitator._note: spec #26. What the facilitator's desk does the instant a round finishes, without being asked -- facilitator/transaction.py hangs it on the engine's round-completed hook, so publication is a consequence of a round ending rather than of somebody running a script ('a manually callable renderer alone does not satisfy this requirement'). The four steps run in the order listed in facilitator.TRANSACTION_STEPS and this list chooses among them; render_edition, publish_editions and notify_group may not be dropped, because they are the requirement rather than a preference, and a config that drops one is refused with spec #26 quoted at it. build_site may be omitted for a deployment that serves the archive some other way -- config.hosting.enabled is the more usual way to say that. editions_label is where the live game's editions land under newspaper.output.editions_dir, beside the sample run's and the recorded playtest's, because spec #27 makes an edition directory append-only and two games cannot share one. notice.channel is what the desk labels the announcement with (the desk composes it and hands it back; it deliberately does not know what the group's inbox is), and notice.include_url decides whether the announcement carries the paper's address -- true is right for a group chat the players are already in, false for a channel a facilitator would rather not paste a credential into, in which case the notice says 'at the usual address'. The address never reaches a committed file either way: Notice.describe() is what gets written down.
facilitator._editions_label_note: Deliberately not the same value as playtest.editions_label -- the recorded game and the live game are two games.

hosting._note: spec #26, #27 -- one fixed URL, not publicly discoverable, with every prior edition still browsable at it. The address is an unguessable subdomain under base_domain, per the fulcra-dashboard pattern: site_id_bytes of randomness become the label, and that label is the entire secret. It is therefore not in this file and not in the repo -- it is read from site_id_env_var if a deployment injects one, else from site_id_file, which .gitignore excludes and hosting/identity.py creates 0600 on first use. Nothing published ever contains it (hosting/guard.py fails the build if anything does), which is why the built site under site_dir is safe to commit: the pages are public, the address is not. `publish` is the curated allowlist of what may be served at all -- a category not named here is not built, and a file whose category is not a known one is a ConfigError rather than a silent inclusion. `front_page` is spec #30a's entry and the one category that may not be dropped: it is the file the address itself answers with, carrying the newest available edition, and a build asked to leave it out is refused rather than serving a 404 at the one URL every mayor holds. `archive_index` is the shelf beside it -- since the front door became the current issue, the list of back issues lives at `archive.html`, and every issue's permanent `round-NN.html` name is untouched (spec #27). `final_edition` and `city_images` are spec #31 and #32's own entries: the last edition is a page of the same paper at the same address, filed under its own category rather than under `editions` because `editions` is checked for one page per round and the final edition shares the last round's number. `privacy` is the delivery policy: robots noindex in three places (robots.txt, a meta tag, and the X-Robots-Tag header) plus the headers that stop a private URL leaking sideways -- no-referrer and a CSP with no external origins, because any off-site request from these pages would put the secret address in somebody else's logs. `publishers` names remote deploy adapters registered in hosting/build.py; it is empty because this deployment has none, so the site is served locally by hosting/serve.py and the build says so in its own provenance rather than implying a deployment that did not happen. Naming an unregistered publisher is a config error, not a quiet fallback.

endgame._note: spec #31-#32. The final edition of The Daily Manifest, published once, when the game ends. The first four flags are the three articles and the material one of them is built from: `crown_cumulative_profit_winner` prints The Crown, `publish_twist_article` prints Consequences, `generate_per_city_description_and_image` prints The Excess with one portrait per city, and `per_city_excess_uses_non_chosen_exports` decides whether a portrait is allowed to describe unchosen offers at all -- false leaves each city described by its public record alone. With all four false there is no final edition rather than an empty one. twist_article_items caps how many consequences the twist article draws from the game's actual arrivals; max_excess_offers_printed_per_city caps how many unchosen offers a portrait reprints (0 prints none, and an offer whose text names a city is withheld at every setting, per spec #21); quote_mayor_answers_per_city caps how many of a city's own answers its portrait quotes, and is additionally gated by facilitator_questions.answers_shared_in_newspaper, which is where that exposure decision is taken. city_image is the portrait's canvas, separate from newspaper.image.width/height because a portrait is not a broadsheet; the *modality* policy is deliberately not separate -- spec #32 says to use #29's raster-preferred/SVG-fallback policy, so portraits resolve through the same newspaper.image.modality_preference and raster_providers rather than through a second copy of it that could disagree. write_private_excess_dossiers is off: a dossier is the one endgame artifact that names which unchosen offers a city *sent*, it is written for that city's own mayor only, and writing it to disk in a repository anybody can read would publish exactly what spec #21 forbids -- see docs/m7-endgame.md.

engine._note: Seeds every random draw the engine makes -- import-need selection, ballot shuffling and profit rolls, each on its own derived stream. null means a genuinely random game, which is what a real game night wants. Set an integer to replay a game move-for-move; the test suite does exactly that. It lives here rather than in code because 'is this game reproducible' is a facilitator's decision, and because a reproducible game is the only way to re-examine a disputed round after the fact.

playtest._note: Where the recorded integration game (playtest/) puts its editions and its built site. Deliberately not `hosting.site_dir`: spec #27 makes an address an append-only archive, so two different games cannot share one. The live game publishes to hosting.site_dir; the recorded game -- eight mayors, seventeen rounds, played by separate agent sessions and replayed from playtest/transcript.json -- publishes here, at its own address, and is committed so the published bytes of a whole game can be read without replaying it. Both are built by the same hosting.build_site under the same privacy policy; only the directory differs.
playtest._editions_note: A label under newspaper.output.editions_dir, beside the scripted sample run's, for the same reason: one directory per game.

roles._note: Generator gets the more creative-leaning model (game content, newspaper prose, city descriptions/images are the bulk of its work). Evaluator gets a model tuned for strict, literal rule-checking against spec.md. Both invoked via `claude --model <alias>`. Revisit if either role's output quality suggests a swap.
